posts.title: Kigali
posts.description: Kigali is the capital of Rwanda and the epicenter of the fight against the government-incited 100-day genocide in 1994 of the Huthi against the Tutsi. They have an impressive museum showing how the Huthi genocide forces were defeated at right this building. They rebuilt, but left one wall with artillery holes as it was. posts.title: Cycling Rwanda
posts.description: At the border, the Rwandan customs officer had me unpack my entire bag, including the dirty laundry bag. Maybe she was searching for plastic bags, which are illegal in Rwanda. When people hear Rwanda they think of the Huthi genocide against the Tutsi, but that was over 30 years ago and Rwanda is now a stable and relatively affluent country. posts.title: Lake Bunyonyi
posts.description: This is a large lake in the southwest of Uganda. Its maximum depth is said to be 900 meters, but Wikipedia is not so sure about that. There are 29 islands, including one to where unmarried pregnant women were banished. It’s called Punishment Island and it’s not much larger than my living room. Punishment indeed.
